meanings.note: Masculine: acteur. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'actress'.

examples.text: Je ne suis pas actrice. Je veux juste voir Mathias.
examples.trans: I'm not an actress. I just want to see Mathias.

meanings.note: Understanding or surprise. Spoken French interj expression meaning 'ah', common in natural conversation.
With things and places. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to like'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aimé').
With people. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to like'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aimé').

examples.text: Tu n'aimais pas Mandelieu? C'est un bel endroit.
examples.trans: Didn't you like Mandelieu? It's a lovely place.

meanings.note: Feminine amoureuse. Masculine noun ('le amoureux', plural 'les amoureux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'boyfriend'.
être amoureux de = to be in love with

examples.text: Françoise avait un amoureux. Devine qui!

examples.trans: Line became a star, and Françoise made art-house films.

meanings.note: Une autre = another (one). Descriptive French adjective meaning 'other'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Also a pronoun. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'other'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je suis seule depuis trois mois.
examples.trans: I've been on my own for three months.

examples.text: Elle n'a pas travaillé depuis deux ans.
examples.trans: She hasn't worked for two years.

meanings.note: The x sounds like z before a vowel. Spoken French num expression meaning 'two', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.

meanings.note: Devine qui! = guess who!. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to guess'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'deviné').

examples.text: Françoise avait un amoureux. Devine qui!
examples.trans: Françoise had a boyfriend. Guess who!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to hate'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'détesté').

meanings.note: je ne veux pas l'entendre = I don't want to hear it
Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to hear'.

examples.trans: I don't want to hear it!

examples.text: Ah bon? Je n'ai jamais entendu ça.

examples.text: Il n'y a rien entre nous.

meanings.note: also as an answer: Exactement! = That's right!

examples.text: Oui, exactement. Le Festival de Cannes.

examples.text: Au fond, Françoise aurait aimé être chanteuse.

meanings.note: c'est l'histoire de... = it's the story of...
Feminine noun ('la histoire', plural 'les histoires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'story'.

examples.text: C'est l'histoire d'un vieux couple qui fait des braquages.
examples.trans: It's the story of an old couple who do hold-ups.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.note: With ne: je ne mens jamais. Invariable French adverb meaning 'never'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Je n'ai jamais vu un acteur aussi exigeant!
examples.trans: I have never seen such a demanding actor!

examples.text: Il ne répond jamais au téléphone pendant le week-end.
examples.trans: He never answers the phone during the weekend.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: Goes before the noun. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'young'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je connais la ministre de la Culture. C'est une jeune femme brillante.
examples.trans: I know the Minister of Culture. She's a brilliant young woman.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le jour', plural 'les jours') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'day'.

examples.text: C'est facile, je sais. Mais je ne pensais pas faire ça un jour.
examples.trans: It's easy, I know. But I never thought I'd do it one day.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

meanings.note: ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'yes'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: parler à quelqu'un = to talk to someone
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to speak'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'parlé').

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: les parts de l'agence = the agency's shares
Feminine noun ('la part', plural 'les parts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'share'.

examples.trans: So I inherit all his shares.

meanings.note: second half of ne... pas; in speech ne is often dropped

meanings.note: With ne: je n'en peux plus. Invariable French adverb meaning 'no more'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
pronounced plys at the end of a sentence in this sense

meanings.note: + infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'can, to be able to'.
conditional: tu pourrais, vous pourriez

examples.trans: On behalf of the agency, I apologise.

meanings.note: c'est moi qui... = I'm the one who...
Qui parle?. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'who'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Tu ne pars pas. C'est moi qui te vire!
